gallery.title: File:Mosaique echansons Bardo.jpg
gallery.description: Mosaic of cupbears, 2nd century CE, from Dougga, at the National Museum of Bardo (Tunisia). It dates from the middle of the 3rd century and depicts a drinking scene: two figures serving drinks to two others, much smaller, from an amphora placed on their shoulders. On the two amphoras are inscribed the formulas PIE ("Drink!" in Latin) and ZHCHC ("You will live" in Greek). On the sides are two other characters bringing another amphora for one, a branch of laurel and a basket of roses for the other. This representation is a form of welcome for the guests and a promise of a good reception. The two slaves carrying wine jars wear typical slave clothing and an amulet against the evil eye on a necklace.

gallery.filename: Dougga Theatre - Looking Down from the Top.jpg
gallery.title: File:Dougga Theatre - Looking Down from the Top.jpg
gallery.credit: Flickr: Tunisia-2739 - Looking Down from the Top
gallery.source: Dougga Theatre - Looking Down from the Top
gallery.description: The theatre of Dougga, which was built in 168 or 169 AD, is one of the best preserved examples in Roman Africa. It could seat 3500 spectators, even though Dougga only had 5000 inhabitants.

gallery.title: File:Baths of the Cyclopes.jpg
gallery.credit: Flickr: Tunisia-2848 - Baths of the Cyclopes
gallery.description: The Baths of the Cyclopes in Dougga is located adjacent to the House of the Trifolium (Brothel). It is a complex of buildings with arched rooms in the basement. The bathrooms are located in the south side of the complex.
